newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber market stable in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber market stable in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices were generally stable in late trading on Friday although sluggish consumer demand continued to dampen market sentiment, traders said.

Traders said a deal was done fob Palembang at 49.375 U.S. cents/lb for June shipment, which was cheaper compared with the offer price of 49.875 in the morning. Offer prices were stable at 49.25 fob Padang, at 49.50 fob Surabaya and at 49.00 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
Traders said offer prices were a little bit higher in Medan at 49.75 against 49.50 in the morning but no deal was done.
"There are no serious buyers in the market and consumer demand is very poor. We expect a bearish trend next week because we don't see any fresh factors which can boost sentiment," said a trader.

Traders said they had not heard news from Malaysia that Chinese buyers were looking to buy SMR20 from Malaysia and SIR20 from Indonesia. "We haven't heard anything about it...maybe because it's been a long time since China has entered our market," said one trader.
Traders said tight supply in north Sumatra failed to improve market sentiment there because buyers were hard to find.
